The saved source discriminant and c4 invariant are

    Delta(s)=6912(1-s)(1+s)^3,

Directly,

    S(1+t)-1=t(9+12t+4t^2),
    (Delta(S(1+t))/t)|_(t=0)=-2^11*3^5,
    c4(S(1))=144.                                  (3)

Thus the discriminant has exactly a simple zero, with p-unit leading
coefficient. In the completed boundary neighbourhood there is a single nodal
fibre; its smooth locus and infinity have no additional degeneracy there.
At t=0 it is

    C: y^2=x^3-3x-2=(x-2)(x+1)^2.                   (4)

Writing u=x+1, its tangent cone at the node is y^2+3u^2. A primitive cube

    R_GM=(1/12)[[-1,-1],[1,1]], R_GM^2=0.            (6)

The corresponding cohomological residue is its transpose, still nilpotent.
The smooth generic identification in LC therefore identifies the source
lattice with the log-crystalline lattice: this uses the following elementary
uniqueness lemma, not an assumption that any regular frame is interchangeable.

**Lemma.** Two logarithmic lattices in one formal differential module over
F((t)), characteristic zero, whose residues are nilpotent, coincide under
their given generic horizontal identification.

To prove it, let P(t) be the horizontal change matrix in GL_n(F((t))) and
n its smallest Laurent exponent. The leading coefficient relation is

    n P_n=R_1 P_n-P_n R_2,                          (7)

up to an overall harmless choice of connection sign. On the space of
matrices, left multiplication by R_1 and right multiplication by R_2 commute
and are nilpotent. Their difference is nilpotent. If n is a nonzero integer,

has no pole. Apply the same argument to P inverse; both matrices are regular,
so P belongs to GL_n(F[[t]]). This proves the lemma, including the requirement
that the actual generic horizontal identification be retained.

actual saved source frame as well. In cohomological column-of-pullbacks

    G=(M^T)^(-1) belongs to GL_2(Q_p[[t]]),

It is precisely that nonzero graph line. Because the node, the component

Its value on the first basis vector is mu. Comparison with the actual
